operation_details.item: The user uses precedent transactions in valuation work.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Hey, how's the quarterly planning going? Seen any interesting deals in the market?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It's busy, but good. I've been pulling together valuation work for the M&A case. Still using DCF as my main approach, and I like to check it with comps. For this one, though, I also pulled precedent transactions to get a sense of what acquirers actually paid.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice, mixing it up. Precedent transactions can give a more tangible market check than multiples sometimes. Did the transaction data align with your DCF?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty closely. The range from transactions was a bit wider, but it helped me sanity-check the assumptions. I always document everything in the memo anyway, so I've got the DCF inputs, comps, and the deal data all laid out.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good practice. That memo's going to be thick. Do you think the board will care more about the transaction comps or the DCF?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Probably the DCF, since that's our primary. But the precedent transactions add credibility because they show real-world pricing, not just model outputs. I'll keep the focus on the DCF but mention the deals as supporting evidence.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Hey, want to grab a coffee later? I could use a break from spreadsheets.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Definitely. Give me ten minutes to finish logging today's assumptions in the memo, and then I'm in.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Forget only that I use precedent transactions, while keeping the DCF, comps, and assumptions documentation.
